_meta.description: SS4O metrics for Secure MCP Gateway — admin-grade coverage. dynamic:false (unmapped fields stay in _source but are not indexed). FIELD GROUPS: OTel core (timestamps, instrument metadata, numeric/histogram values, nested buckets/exemplars); resource attrs; identity tuple (snake_case: user_id/user_email/project_id/project_name/project_registry/org_id/gateway_name/gateway_version/server_name/tool_name); operational ids (mcp_config_id/custom_id/request_id/correlation_id/session_id — request_id/correlation_id/session_id enable trace-metric correlation via exemplars and per-request slicing; expect medium-to-high cardinality so use carefully in aggregations); existing categoricals (outcome/direction/status_code/provider/check_kind/violation_type/block_reason/failure_reason/cache/result); health & registry; guardrail labels (guardrail_name/server_tools_guardrail_name/validation_mode/kind/operation_type); per-call detector signal (detector/detector_subtype/detector_enabled/detector_blocked/compliance_framework/compliance_label/pii_category/pii_entity_type/topic_detected/policy_blocked/bias_detected); cloud gateway_id; sandbox; request-type discriminators (request_type/source_event/source_name/mcp_method); I/O mode flags; OAuth (oauth_version/grant_type/use_mtls/is_remote); timeout (escalation_level/cancelled); session pool (session_reused/session_pool_enabled/tools_source); MCP protocol (mcp_protocol_version/mcp_capability/capability_outcome/mcp_notification_method); tool annotations (destructive/read_only/idempotent/open_world_hint); admin/audit (admin_action/action/actor/source/auth_via/authorized_via/surface/resource_type/resource_id/command/subcommand/exit_code/confirmed/operation); HTTP RED (http.route/method/status_code/status_class/service/error.type/error_class/reason); connection lifecycle (event/transport_type/server_health_state/eviction_reason/error_kind); reliability (subsystem/failed_step/component/retry_attempt/degradation_mode/circuit_breaker_state/recovery_strategy/error_code/severity/failure_reason_class); outbound HTTP (host/upstream/cloud_endpoint/cache_result); telemetry pipeline (signal/exporter); process (process_role/process/generation/version); lifecycle (trigger/shutdown_reason/include_tool_cache/plugin_type/plugin_name); config (entity/path_hash); cache backend (cache_backend/redis_operation/redis_host/connection_state); security (window_minutes/checkpoint/pattern/pattern_hash); flat numeric attrs (duration_ms/duration_seconds/latency_ms/elapsed_ms/elapsed_seconds/size_bytes/bytes_sent/bytes_received — these are NON-OTel-native shape, useful when a dashboard or downstream tool expects latency/size as a flat metric.attributes.* field rather than the canonical OTel histogram instrument shape where the value lives in the standard `value`/`sum`/`count`/`bucketCounts` fields and the metric NAME differentiates the operation; emit only when explicitly required by an external dashboard contract, otherwise prefer the OTel-native histogram instruments listed below). EXPECTED METRIC INSTRUMENT NAMES (all ride on the `name` keyword field — the metric NAME *is* how latencies/sizes/counts are differentiated, attributes only label the data points): LATENCY HISTOGRAMS (the gateway emits a dedicated histogram per operation type — value = duration, unit = `s` or `ms` as declared per instrument): enkrypt.tool.duration, enkrypt.guardrail.duration, enkrypt.guardrail.detector_score, enkrypt.health.duration, enkrypt.discovery.per_server.duration, enkrypt.playground.registry_lookup.duration, enkrypt.playground.consumer_info_lookup.duration, enkrypt.mcp.connection.handshake.duration, enkrypt.mcp.initialize.duration, enkrypt.mcp.http.duration, enkrypt.api.duration, enkrypt.session.pool.idle_seconds, enkrypt.timeout.duration, enkrypt.config.reload.duration, enkrypt.oauth.token.latency, enkrypt.cli.duration, enkrypt.system.backup.duration, enkrypt.system.restore.duration, enkrypt.http.client.duration, enkrypt.admin.cache_flush.duration, enkrypt.config.validation.duration, python.gc.duration, enkrypt.asyncio.event_loop.lag. SIZE HISTOGRAMS: enkrypt.cloud.api.bytes_sent, enkrypt.cloud.api.bytes_received, enkrypt.api.request_body_size, enkrypt.api.response_body_size, enkrypt.mcp.http.request_size, enkrypt.mcp.http.response_size, enkrypt.tool.calls_per_request, enkrypt.telemetry.export.batch_size.
